proof_summary: A binomial identity and the Fibonacci sum formula give \(2nS(n)=L_{2n}-1\), so integrality would imply \(2n\mid L_{2n}-1\). Residues modulo \(4\) and \(5\) eliminate the cases where \(n\) has a factor \(2,3,\) or \(5\); otherwise, for the least prime divisor \(p\ge7\), roots of \(x^2-x-1\) in a splitting field modulo \(p\) and a multiplicative-order argument force their order to be \(12\), whence \(p\mid L_{12}-2=320\), a contradiction.
